jordan: Hey — reproducing a strange case in the streaming sample app. If the client disconnects mid-stream and reconnects, sometimes we get interleaved/misaligned chunks (e.g. '}}\n{"partial"' halves). Anyone seen this?

maria: yup saw similar on iOS sample. Sometimes resume token gets applied twice and the client replays a tail fragment.

eric: can you paste a raw capture? curious if it's SSE framing (\n\n delim) vs last-event-id handling.

jordan: here's trimmed capture:
```
data: {"id":"abc","chunk":"{\"text\":\"First part\""}

````

sam: looks like the client treats a partial JSON fragment as a full data event when reconnecting. We added a safety check in py/go SDKs to buffer until valid JSON. mobile wasn't patched.

maria: on mobile it's tricky because the OS socket close -> reconnect flow can yield an extra `\n` which the parser consumes as empty event. That can shift boundary detection.

eric: two possible fixes:
 1) treat `data:` chunks as raw stream fragments and only attempt JSON parse once full balanced braces seen (count { vs }).
 2) use resume token/last_event_id semantics and send `?resume_after=<offset>` so server truncates duplicate tail.

jordan: could be a race where server re-sends last N tokens and client also kept KV cache prefix. So duplicate prefix + new suffix -> misalignment.

sam: i'll open a tiny patch to the sample app to add a reassembly buffer + unit test for mismatched boundaries. sampleapp will now check `isBalancedJson(buffer)` before emit. patch ready in branch `devex/stream-reassembly`.

deploy-bot: Staging deployment started for branch devex/stream-reassembly (build #4821).

maria: thanks. can we also add a flaky test that simulates mid-stream TCP close and immediate reconnect? caught a couple of regressions earlier.

sam: good idea. i'll add a harness that injects partial chunks + dup resume tokens.

jordan: awesome — once staged I'll try the mobile sample again and report results. thx :thumbsup:
